scenario.name: Terminator EDR Killer Abusing Signed Zemana AntiMalware Driver (zam64.sys / CVE-2021-31728)
scenario.overview: Imagine a burglar carrying a genuinely stamped security-vendor master badge bought from an underground broker. After dropping that legitimate badge into the building engine room, the burglar walks up to an unguarded badge-enrollment desk that forgets to check identity, writes their own badge number onto the VIP master roster, and then walks in an endless loop shutting off every security camera and guard station across the building. In this scenario (T1068, Terminator EDR Killer Abusing Signed Zemana AntiMalware Driver (zam64.sys / CVE-2021-31728)), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: dropping Randomized Signed Zemana Driver, then self-Allowlisting Caller PID, then continuous Ring-0 Termination Loop via IOCTL. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Dropping Randomized Signed Zemana Driver, then Self-Allowlisting Caller PID, then Continuous Ring-0 Termination Loop via IOCTL, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 6 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Dropping Randomized Signed Zemana Driver (zam64.sys) into System32\drivers
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation & Defense Evasion (T1068 / T1036.005)
stages.description: Holding administrator keys, the burglar unpacks a genuinely signed third-party security driver, stamps a random cover name onto its tag so simple filename checklists overlook it, and plugs it straight into the building core engine room. When executed with administrator privileges, Terminator.exe wrote an embedded copy of zam64.sys (a kernel driver validly signed by Zemana Ltd. and countersigned by Microsoft) into C:\Windows\System32\drivers\ using a randomly generated 5-to-10 character .sys filename (evading naive detection rules that only check if the file path ends in zam64.sys) and started the kernel service via the Service Control Manager. Regardless of the randomized .sys filename on disk, the driver’s DriverEntry routine always creates the fixed device symbolic link \\.\ZemanaAntiMalware (or \\.\B94B8021-5217-4091-96E5-6353272B9429). Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ Stage 1: Dropping Randomized Signed Zemana Driver (zam64.sys) into System32\drivers / ⇠#1 ACK 6) from Node ① (#1 Terminator.exe User-Mode Binary) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 IOCTL 0x80002048 Ring-0 Process Kill).

stages.title: Stage 2: Self-Allowlisting Caller PID via Unauthenticated IOCTL 0x80002010 (CVE-2021-31728)
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1068 - Exploitation for Privilege Escalation)
stages.description: Even though the driver only obeys badge numbers written on its VIP security roster, its enrollment window never checks who is asking to be added. The burglar simply taps the enrollment code and writes their own badge number straight onto the VIP list. Although zam64.sys checks an internal allowlist of trusted Process IDs before permitting privileged operations like process termination or raw disk access, it exposes IOCTL 0x80002010 (IOCTL_REGISTER_PROCESS, tracked as CVE-2021-31728, which accepts any 4-byte DWORD Process ID from user mode and appends it to the driver’s Ring-0 trusted process table without verifying the caller’s executable signature). Terminator.exe simply passed GetCurrentProcessId() to 0x80002010 to authorize itself. Once a PID is registered via 0x80002010, zam64.sys unlocks its full suite of administrative IOCTLs, including process termination, registry manipulation, and direct SCSI/disk read-write, for that caller. In the documented EDR exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to Signed Zemana Driver (zam64.sys), Signed Zemana Driver (zam64.sys) responds with ALERT T1068 (confirming that the Stage 2: Self-Allowlisting Caller PID via Unauthenticated IOCTL 0x80002010 (CVE-2021-31728) request succeeded on Signed Zemana Driver (zam64.sys) and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 Stage 3: Continuous Ring-0 Termination Loop via IOCTL 0x80002048). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ Stage 2: Self-Allowlisting Caller PID via Unauthenticated IOCTL 0x80002010 (CVE-2021-31728) / ⇠#2 ALERT T1068) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Signed Zemana Driver (zam64.sys)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 IOCTL 0x80002048 Ring-0 Process Kill).

stages.title: Stage 3: Continuous Ring-0 Termination Loop via IOCTL 0x80002048
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1562.001 - Disable or Modify Tools)
stages.description: Now accepted as a VIP security supervisor, the burglar paces the hallways in a relentless circle, comparing every guard uniform against a pocket hit-list of 24 known security agencies and flipping the master kill switch on every matching guard before they can sound the alarm. In an infinite while (true) loop, Terminator.exe called CreateToolhelp32Snapshot to enumerate active processes, compared each executable name against a hardcoded array of 24 security vendors (CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Defender, Sophos, Cortex XDR, Kaspersky, McAfee, Trend Micro, etc.), and sent IOCTL 0x80002048 with the matching PID (causing zam64.sys to call ZwTerminateProcess from Ring 0 and bypass User-Mode PPL protections). Modern EDRs neutralize Terminator prior to 0x80002048 by blocking the load of zam64.sys at NtLoadDriver / DriverLoad time using behavioral prevention and kernel blocklists. In the documented EDR exchange from Signed Zemana Driver (zam64.sys) to IOCTL 0x80002010 Allowlist Bypass, IOCTL 0x80002010 Allowlist Bypass responds with ALERT T1562.001 (confirming that the Stage 3: Continuous Ring-0 Termination Loop via IOCTL 0x80002048 request succeeded on IOCTL 0x80002010 Allowlist Bypass and completing the final execution objective of Terminator EDR Killer Abusing Signed Zemana AntiMalware Driver (zam64.sys / CVE-2021-31728)). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ Stage 3: Continuous Ring-0 Termination Loop via IOCTL 0x80002048 / ⇠#3 ALERT T1562.001) from Node ③ (#3 Signed Zemana Driver (zam64.sys)) to Node ④ (#4 IOCTL 0x80002010 Allowlist Bypass), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 IOCTL 0x80002048 Ring-0 Process Kill).
